reflections.title: "Walk by the Spirit"

reflect.text: Every Christian knows the tug-of-war inside the heart. When we are united to Jesus, we receive new life, but our old sinful desires do not disappear overnight. As Joe Rigney points out, the Christian life begins by recognizing this daily clash between our old nature and God's Spirit.

This inner battle lasts as long as we are in this world, but we do not fight alone. Jesus is our almighty helper who watches over us in every struggle. As we surrender our self-will to Him, Christ's life takes root in us, producing good fruit naturally instead of through strained human effort.

questions: When you feel a tug toward selfish habits, how can you pause and ask the Holy Spirit for help?
What helps you remember that Jesus is with you in the daily struggle against sin?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for giving us Your Holy Spirit to guide us every day. Help us surrender our selfish desires and yield to Your power when temptation comes. Grow Your peaceful, loving fruit in our lives as we trust in You. Amen.

D5.author: Joe Rigney
D5.work: Walk the War Before You: What It Means to Live by the Spirit

unsupported.text: Scripture promises that when we walk by the Spirit, we will not give in to those wrong cravings. The Holy Spirit acts within us to stop the spread of sin, much like an antiseptic stops an infection. He interrupts our selfish thoughts, calms our inner battles, and gently reshapes what we desire.
unsupported.problem: Neither D4, D5, nor the passage teaches that the Holy Spirit 'calms our inner battles'; rather, they describe an ongoing, active conflict and warfare between the Spirit and the flesh.

reflections.title: "Live by the Spirit"

reflect.text: In the Christian life, believing in Jesus and walking with Jesus belong together. Faith in Christ is the solid foundation of a building, and a holy life is the house built upon it. We cannot have a safe shelter without a strong foundation, and a foundation without walls gives no shelter in a storm.

Walking in step with the Spirit means remembering that the Holy Spirit is a real person, God's own loving presence living with us. He is not just an impersonal force. Walking with Him means turning away from selfish habits and asking Him each day to direct our choices.

Charles Spurgeon taught that when "faith and life be put together," our walk with God becomes strong and lasting. As we yield our hearts to the Spirit's control, He produces Christlike virtues in us and helps us live in peace and unity with other believers.

questions: How does your trust in Jesus provide the foundation for how you treat others each day?
In what area of your life do you need to ask the Holy Spirit to guide your steps today?
reflections.prayer: Holy Spirit, thank You for making Your home in our hearts and giving us new life. Teach us to put our faith into practice by turning away from sin and following Your gentle guidance. Unite us in love with our brothers and sisters in Christ as we walk with You. Amen.

D6.author: Jeremy Linneman
D6.work: What Does It Mean to Walk in the Spirit?

reflections.title: Led by the Spirit into Grace

reflect.text: When we read about the fight against sin and the works of the flesh, we might feel tempted to measure ourselves by God's law. But looking at our own performance from a legal viewpoint will only lead to despair. God's law shows us our shortcomings, and no human being can earn acceptance with God by trying to keep rules.

Being led by the Spirit means we no longer live under the heavy burden of the law. Instead, we live in the freedom of grace, which is God's kindness that we do not deserve. When we wonder about our standing with God, the real question is not whether we are perfect in ourselves, but whether we are accepted in Christ.

When doubts trouble our minds, we must look to the cross rather than to our own weak feelings. As Charles Spurgeon wrote, "Judge yourself at what Christ is rather than at what you are." God's promises never fail, and the Spirit frees us from fear so we can rest securely in Jesus.

questions: When you feel discouraged by your shortcomings, how does resting in God's grace bring you peace?
Why is it better to look at what Christ has done for you instead of focusing on your own performance?
reflections.prayer: Heavenly Father, thank You that we are saved by Your grace and not by our own rule-keeping. When we are troubled by our weaknesses, help us fix our eyes on Jesus and His complete work on the cross. Teach us to walk in the freedom and joy of Your Holy Spirit. Amen.
